newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to mull scrapping secret bank accounts.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to mull scrapping secret bank accounts.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has ordered a study to decide whether to rescind a decree allowing anonymous hard currency accounts at commercial banks, a tax official said on Friday.

"The president has told the government and central bank to analyse and draw conclusions on the expediency of allowing the decree to continue to apply," Olexander Kabanets, deputy head of the tax inspectorate's currency control department, said.
The decree, signed in August 1995, was meant to attract funds that had been invested abroad back to the former Soviet republic.
"There was great hope our citizens holding cash abroad would respond, but this hope turned out to be unjustified," he said.
"I am certain the decree will be annulled as it gives the state nothing. We cannot find out how much money is there or apply taxes."
Tax authorities have prepared a new decree imposing severe sanctions for failing to return hard currency or hiding profits from hard currency investments abroad.
Kabanets said that Ukrainian enterprises and organisations had invested 9.3 billion hryvnias abroad.
The state earned only 138 million hryvnias last year in dividends from investments abroad, instead of the 1.3 billion hryvnias it had anticipated, he said. ($ = 1.83 hryvnias)
